To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inclusion of chiral N2LO three-nucleon interactions leads to a strong reduction of regulator dependence of neutron matter predictions with chiral N3 LO two-nucleon forces.

the regulator dependence of neutron matter predictions can be strongly reduced with the inclusion of three-body forces, that this reduction is most effective when using chiral interactions that are consistent at the two- and three-nucleon level, and that the regulator dependence can be further reduced when employing a regulator that is consistent with the power counting.
the cutoff dependence of neutron matter predictions with chiral interactions is strongly reduced by the inclusion of consistent three-nucleon interactions, which is in line with previous findings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the energy per neutron in neutron matter.
the development of a perturbative approach to neutron matter based on realistic chiral nuclear forces.
the investigation of the dependence of nuclear observables on the choice of the cutoff scale and the regulator function in the framework of effective chiral nuclear forces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cutoff dependence of the results is reduced, and that the regulator dependence of the predictions can be significantly reduced by including three-body forces.
, with the inclusion of three-body forces, the regulator dependence is reduced by a factor of about 10 compared to the case of two-nucleon forces only.

the inclusion of N3LO 2NFs and N2LO 3NFs in neutron matter calculations with the same regulators leads to a reduced dependence of the results on the choice of regulator, but the regulator dependence is not eliminated completely.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inclusion of chiral three-nucleon interactions is essential for the calculation of neutron matter properties.

the regulator dependence is reduced by about 50% for all regulators, and that the regulator dependence of the energy per particle is reduced by about a factor of 2 for the regulator of Ref. [ 1 ] and by more than an order of magnitude for the regulators of Refs. [ 2, 3 ].
perturbative chemo-physical predictions with chiral two- and three-body forces are more stable against the regulator choice than the corresponding results obtained with phenomenological interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given chiral two-body interaction, the regulator dependence of the predictions for the energy per particle is reduced by more than a factor of 3 when three-body forces are taken into account.
, in order to obtain a cutoff-independent result for the energy per particle, the regulator dependence has to be taken into account when calculating two- and three-body contributions separately.
, in contrast to two-body potentials, three-body forces are less affected by the regulator dependence.
